confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one web search of aggregated cost-of-living sites (mylifeelsewhere, nomad.watch, livingcost, citycost, traveltables and others). Those sources gave a cheap meal at about $5, a mid-range dinner for two at about $20, a cappuccino at $1.80 to $3 and a draft beer at about $4.70 (range $2.76 to $6.62). I raised the mid-range meal a little because the July 2026 window is peak tourist season. Alcohol is only sold in licensed venues, mostly ones aimed at tourists, so drinks cost more than local food. Cocktails and wine are less certain: I estimated them from their usual price relative to beer at licensed Moroccan venues, not from direct sources. The accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge of Essaouira's medina hostels, riads and three-star hotels, with a summer premium added. I did not search for or check any booking listings. The FX rate is the RBA AUD/USD rate of 0.6720 at 4:00 pm on 18 November 2026. It came from a search result summary that pointed to the RBA exchange rates page, and I did not read the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other Moroccan tourist towns, especially Marrakech and Agadir. Essaouira's restaurant prices are usually somewhat lower than Marrakech's but rise in summer.
